entry.note: Identified from the arXiv title page (arXiv:1210.5756v1, math.MG, 21 Oct 2012): Bezdek and Reid, 'Contact graphs of unit sphere packings revisited', 19 pp, 13 sections. No ref() entry existed (references.ts had no packing entry). Entry bezdek-reid2013 created 2026-09-06; no citation site yet — bib orphan pending the cite-in-block bean.

relevance.rationale: The lead to check was that the contact-number bounds bear on QOU.Mass.CoordinationSaturation (bounded-degree coordination, bean qou-brng). Verified against the text: Theorem 1(i) (p. 2, proved in §2 via Hales' 13-ball separation, Theorem 5, and an isoperimetric bound on the union of enlarged balls) gives touching pairs < 6n − 0.926 n^{2/3} for ANY packing of n ≥ 2 unit balls in E^3; Theorem 1(ii) < 6n − 3.665 n^{2/3} for lattice packings; and fcc packings with n = (2k^3+k)/3 balls achieve > 6n − 7.862 n^{2/3}. That is precisely the affine-plus-sub-affine shape the corpus's saturation model assumes — bulk term 6n = 12·n/2 from the kissing number 12 (bounded degree k = 12) and a surface deficit ∝ n^{2/3} — and it brackets the coefficient of the n^{2/3} surface term the corpus computes for fcc facets in docs/audits/2026-09-05-coordination-surface-deficit.md. Theorem 2 (touching triplets ≤ 25n/3, quadruples ≤ 11n/4) bounds the higher-body-order contact counts that QOU.MassTheory.BodyOrderRecurrenceDepth says the extensive term needs (depth ≥ 3), IF a geometric packing model is adopted. Why not 'core': the corpus already declined to cite exactly these forms on principle (docs/audits/2026-09-05-max-contact-sub-affine-negative.md §5 — qou-rav3 demands an internal packing argument; the ambient geometry is hyperbolic and using it consistently costs 2.64x; three-dimensionality is derived nowhere; the exponent is imported). Bezdek–Reid is Euclidean and settles none of those; it converts an unreferenced import into a referenced one. Also verified: Theorems 4/5 (§2) are where the kissing-number-12 rigidity enters, via Hales' result that a 13th ball must sit at distance ≥ 2.52 — so the 'k = 12' of the Lean has a theorem behind it here, not only a picture. Scope-(a) on the negative half: this document does not derive coordination from the framework; it constrains what any Euclidean-packing realisation of it could give.

keyResults.locator: Theorem 1(i), p. 2; proof §2 (Theorem 4, Corollary 2, isoperimetric step)
keyResults.statement: The number of touching pairs in an arbitrary packing of n ≥ 2 unit balls in E^3 is less than 6n − 0.926 n^{2/3}.
keyResults.useForFolio: The held, sharp form of the bounded-degree (k = 12) plus sub-affine surface-deficit shape that QOU.Mass.CoordinationSaturation and 2026-09-05-coordination-surface-deficit.md assume; cite it where the corpus currently says 'geometric close-packing count'. It makes the Euclidean import citable, not derived — the four recorded objections stand.

keyResults.locator: Theorem 1(ii) and the fcc lower bound quoted from Bezdek [2] on p. 2 (n = (2k^3+k)/3)
keyResults.statement: Lattice packings have fewer than 6n − 3.665 n^{2/3} touching pairs, while explicit fcc clusters have more than 6n − 7.862 n^{2/3}.
keyResults.useForFolio: Brackets the coefficient of the n^{2/3} surface term for fcc clusters, [0.926, 7.862] in general and [3.665, 7.862] for lattices — a cross-check target for the fcc-facet surface-deficit coefficients the corpus tabulates.

keyResults.locator: Theorem 2(i)–(iii), p. 2; §4–§6 (Theorem 3: ≤ 25 touching pairs / ≤ 11 triplets among caps of angular radius π/6 on S^2)
keyResults.statement: Touching triplets (resp. quadruples) in a packing of n unit balls in E^3 number at most 25n/3 (resp. 11n/4); fcc clusters realise > 8n − 12(3n/2)^{2/3} + 4n^{1/3} triplets.
keyResults.useForFolio: Bounds the 3- and 4-body contact counts a geometric realisation of the extensive term would carry, relevant to the body-order depth ≥ 3 forcing (QOU.MassTheory.BodyOrderRecurrenceDepth) and the 3-body cumulant sign result (QOU.MassTheory.MayerThreeBodySign); a constraint on any packing model, not a derivation.
